activities.l3: Locate Facilities Access information and the applicable form
activities.description: The applicant finds the Facilities Access page on the public website and follows the outbound hyperlink to the iApply forms platform.

activities.l3: Determine which submission type applies
activities.description: The applicant decides whether the request is a new Expression of Interest, a Variation, a Notification of Works or a Decommissioning. The variation form is not linked from the website, so most variations are lodged on the Expression of Interest form.

activities.l3: Identify the SAPN asset the request relates to
activities.description: The applicant identifies the pole, structure, pit, kiosk or fence, ordinarily by transcribing the asset number from the plate. Asset locations exist in GIS but are not exposed for external selection, so a desk-based applicant often works from a street view.

activities.l3: Complete the submission form
activities.description: The applicant completes the online form — 38 fields for an Expression of Interest across applicant, location, equipment, attachment and declaration sections, with no conditional logic beyond three fields and no save and resume.

activities.l3: Attach supporting evidence
activities.description: The applicant attaches site photographs, the equipment specification sheet, engineering drawings where required, the certificate of currency for public liability insurance, and evidence of council consultation where applicable.

activities.l3: Submit the declaration and lodge the request
activities.description: The applicant signs the declaration and submits. The submission generates a PDF which is delivered by SMTP to the Facilities Access shared mailbox; oversize mail bounces from the mail server after submission.

activities.l3: Lodge on the applicant's behalf where assistance is needed
activities.description: Where an applicant cannot complete the online form, a Facilities Access Officer or Contact Centre Agent completes it during a call. The applicant confirms the declaration verbally and this is noted.

activities.l3: Issue the automated acknowledgement
activities.description: The platform issues an auto-acknowledgement to the applicant containing the reference number. It confirms receipt only and is not authorisation to proceed.

activities.l3: Process the shared mailbox queue
activities.description: The Facilities Access Officer opens the shared mailbox on the next business day and works through items in order of receipt, separating new submissions from applicant replies, chasers and internal mail.

activities.l3: Record the submission in the Facilities Access Tracker
activities.description: The Officer creates a row recording reference, date received, applicant organisation, contact details, asset IDs, equipment type and channel of receipt, by re-keying from the PDF. Measured at 6 minutes 40 seconds per submission.

activities.l3: File the submission and attachments in the document library
activities.description: The Officer saves the submission PDF and all attachments to a folder named by reference, applicant and suburb, and sets the Tracker status to In Triage.

activities.l3: Verify applicant identity and ABN
activities.description: The Officer confirms the legal entity name and that the ABN is active on ABR lookup, and that where the applicant is not the equipment owner the party they act for is named.

activities.l3: Validate each asset ID against GIS
activities.description: The Officer confirms each stated Asset ID in GIS. The most common failure at about one in five submissions; where the intent is clear from photographs and address the Officer identifies the correct asset and records the correction.

activities.l3: Verify insurance currency and level of cover
activities.description: The Officer opens the certificate of currency and checks by eye that public liability cover of at least $20,000,000 is current at the date of submission. About one in six is expired or for the wrong amount.

activities.l3: Verify equipment and attachment detail is complete
activities.description: The Officer confirms equipment type, make, model, dimensions, mass and projected wind area, and the proposed mounting height, method and orientation. Wind area is optional on the form and is absent about 70% of the time.

activities.l3: Verify third-party consent and council consultation
activities.description: Where the asset is on council land or the proposal has visual amenity impact, the Officer confirms evidence of council consultation is present.

activities.l3: Verify the notifying party's authority to act
activities.description: For a Notification of Works, the Officer confirms the notifying party is the Licence Holder or is authorised by them. The form captures the party acted for as free text and there is no systematic verification; the check relies on the Officer's familiarity with the parties.

activities.l3: Classify the request and re-route where the wrong form was used
activities.description: The Officer determines whether the request is genuinely a new Expression of Interest, a Variation or maintenance access, and re-routes it. Approximately 60% of change requests are ultimately assessed as like-for-like.

activities.l3: Issue a consolidated request for information
activities.description: Where any check fails, the Officer emails the applicant listing every deficiency in a single message and records the date of the request. Sequential partial requests are not permitted.

activities.l3: Follow up at 14 and 28 days and escalate at 90
activities.description: The Officer follows up where no response is received and escalates to the Team Leader for a closure decision at 90 calendar days. There is no automated closure and submissions have remained open for eleven months.

activities.l3: Stop the turnaround clock while awaiting applicant information
activities.description: Time spent in Awaiting Applicant Information is excluded from SAPN turnaround measurement.

activities.l3: Set and maintain the submission status
activities.description: The Officer maintains the submission's state in the Tracker, which is the record of truth for status. The status column is free text and holds 47 distinct values conflating status, assignment and blocked-reason.

activities.l3: Handle applicant status enquiries
activities.description: Applicants seeking status contact the shared mailbox or the Contact Centre. The Contact Centre has no visibility of the Tracker and can only take a message and email the Facilities Access team.

activities.l3: Refer the complete submission to Network Standards
activities.description: The Officer emails the network standards mailbox with the reference number and a link to the document folder, and sets the Tracker status to Under Engineering Assessment.

activities.l3: Claim the assessment from the shared queue
activities.description: Assessment is picked up from the shared queue by any available Network Standards Engineer, who records their name against the reference to prevent duplicate assessment. Two engineers occasionally assess the same submission.

activities.l3: Screen the proposal against the Standard Envelope
activities.description: The Engineer tests the proposal against eight criteria — asset type and construction, clearance, mass under 25 kg, wind area under 0.3 square metres, fewer than three existing attachments, asset condition, distance from a substation, and no supply requirement — to decide between a desktop check and full assessment.

activities.l3: Retrieve all approved installations on the asset
activities.description: The Engineer retrieves every approved installation on the asset before assessing, so that cumulative loading is considered rather than only the incremental change. This requires a manual search of the Tracker by asset ID.

activities.l3: Assess structural loading and clearance to live conductors
activities.description: The Engineer assesses structural loading against TS-220 and clearance against TS-115, determining the clearance from what is actually on the pole. Attachments are opened in separate windows and the arithmetic is performed by hand.

activities.l3: Conduct a site inspection where the desktop assessment is insufficient
activities.description: About 15% of Expressions of Interest require a physical inspection. It is arranged by email with no scheduling, and the only record is the Engineer's notes and photographs taken on a personal phone.

activities.l3: Record the determination and categorised reason
activities.description: The Engineer records one of four outcomes — Approved as Proposed, Approved with Conditions, Design Change Required, or Rejected — with a categorised reason from a nine-value list plus supporting narrative for anything other than approval as proposed.

activities.l3: Select conditions from the Standard Conditions Library
activities.description: Conditions are selected from the fifteen-condition library wherever a standard condition fits, covering attachment height, supervision, access permits, removal on demand, labelling, inspection frequency and reinstatement.

activities.l3: Peer-review any free-text condition before issue
activities.description: Free-text conditions may be added where no standard condition applies and must be reviewed by a second engineer before issue.

activities.l3: Issue the determination to the applicant
activities.description: The Officer issues the outcome to the applicant. Where a design change is required, the required changes are stated specifically and the status is set to Awaiting Applicant Information.

activities.l3: Reassess a revised proposal as a further cycle
activities.description: On receipt of a revised proposal the completeness check is repeated and the submission returns to the same engineer where available. The reassessment is recorded as a further cycle against the same reference; submissions exceeding three cycles are escalated.

activities.l3: Determine and raise the assessment fee
activities.description: On determination the Officer raises the assessment fee per the current Schedule of Facilities Access Fees, standard or complex according to whether a full structural assessment or site inspection was required. Assessment fees are payable regardless of outcome, including rejection.

activities.l3: Approve a fee waiver where the applicant is eligible
activities.description: Fee waivers require Team Leader approval and are ordinarily limited to community groups, emergency services and local government non-commercial installations.

activities.l3: Request preparation of the Licence Agreement
activities.description: The Officer emails Legal and Commercial with the licence holder legal entity and ABN, asset IDs, equipment schedule, approved conditions, term and fee schedule.

activities.l3: Prepare the agreement from the legal template
activities.description: Legal and Commercial prepare the agreement from the TMP-FA-07 Word template, reproducing the approved conditions in full. Conditions are reproduced by hand rather than merged from structured data.

activities.l3: Issue the agreement for digital signature
activities.description: The agreement is uploaded manually and issued to the Licence Holder for execution, and the Tracker status is set to Awaiting Agreement.

activities.l3: Execute the Licence Agreement
activities.description: The Licence Holder executes the agreement by digital signature. This is the longest stage in the process at typically four to eight weeks, and longer where the applicant's legal representatives seek amendments to the template.

activities.l3: File the executed agreement and record the approval
activities.description: On receipt of the executed agreement the Officer files it against the reference and sets the Tracker status to Approved. The installation may then proceed.

activities.l3: Notify practical completion of the installation
activities.description: The Licence Holder is required to notify SAPN within 10 business days of completing the installation.

activities.l3: Record the completion date and create the installation record
activities.description: The Officer records the completion date and establishes the installation record with its asset IDs, licence holder, equipment schedule and approved conditions. Approximately 1,000 approved Expressions of Interest have no matching installation record.

activities.l3: Commence the annual licence fee from the completion date
activities.description: Annual attachment licence fees commence from the date of practical completion, not the date of approval, and are indexed annually per attachment.

activities.l3: Lodge the Notification of Works within the minimum lead time
activities.description: The Notifying Party lodges not less than 5 business days before routine works, 10 where isolation or switching is required, and 15 where traffic management on an arterial road is needed. Most notifications are lodged by contractors rather than by Licence Holders.

activities.l3: Register the notification and issue the acknowledgement
activities.description: The Officer records the notification in the Tracker on the same business day and sends the acknowledgement template. The acknowledgement confirms receipt only and must not be capable of being read as authorisation.

activities.l3: Check the notification against the licence and its conditions
activities.description: The Officer confirms the notification references a current licence in Approved status, that the asset IDs match the licence, that the works are maintenance rather than a variation, and that relevant licence conditions have been acknowledged. Conditions are held only in PDFs, so the condition check is not executable as written.

activities.l3: Actively pursue a deficient notification
activities.description: Where a validity check fails the Officer contacts the Notifying Party the same business day by phone where the start date is within 5 business days, and by email otherwise. Deficient notifications are pursued rather than queued.

activities.l3: Refer the valid notification to Field Services
activities.description: All valid notifications are referred to the Works Coordinator by email and the status is set to Under Review.

activities.l3: Check the notified asset and dates against the switching program
activities.description: The Works Coordinator checks the switching program in SODS for low voltage and ADMS for high voltage, scheduled planned interruptions, SAPN construction and maintenance work, vegetation management, and other third-party notifications on the same asset. Response is within 2 business days, or 5 where isolation is requested.

activities.l3: Resolve a clash by rescheduling or coordinated attendance
activities.description: Where a conflict exists the third party reschedules, SAPN work is adjusted, or both parties attend under coordination arrangements specified by the Works Coordinator, which become conditions of clearance. Where an SAPN interruption already exists, coordinated attendance is generally preferred.

activities.l3: Incorporate an isolation request into the switching program
activities.description: Where isolation is requested the notification is referred to Network Standards and incorporated into the switching program, which is prepared on a rolling fortnightly cycle. Clearance is conditional on the switching plan being approved.

activities.l3: Issue clearance stating assets, dates and conditions
activities.description: On a clear conflict check the Officer issues clearance stating the reference, assets cleared, date range, conditions of clearance including those carried from the licence, any access permit reference, on-site contact details and the obligation to notify completion.

activities.l3: Attend site within the cleared range
activities.description: Clearance is limited to the assets, dates and works described. It does not authorise attendance outside the range, works on an unlisted asset, any variation, or entry into the exclusion zone without a separately issued access permit.

activities.l3: Advise completion or non-attendance
activities.description: The Notifying Party is required to advise completion or non-attendance within 2 business days of the end of the cleared range. Compliance is estimated at under 50%.

activities.l3: Close the notification and record the access
activities.description: The Officer records the outcome and closes the notification as Completed or Not Attended. Where no advice is received notifications are closed administratively at month end, which degrades the accuracy of access records.

activities.l3: Contact Network Control on the published 24-hour number
activities.description: Where equipment failure has caused or will imminently cause loss of a service that cannot await standard lead time, the Notifying Party contacts Network Control directly, bypassing the Facilities Access team. Commercial inconvenience alone does not constitute an emergency.

activities.l3: Assess network risk and grant or refuse verbal authorisation
activities.description: Network Control confirms the caller's identity and the affected installation, assesses the network risk, and grants or refuses verbal authorisation, recording the time, authorising controller, party authorised, asset and any conditions in the control log.

activities.l3: Lodge the retrospective notification within 2 business days
activities.description: The Notifying Party is required to lodge a retrospective notification marked as emergency, referencing the verbal authorisation. Compliance is estimated at approximately 40%.

activities.l3: Reconcile the control log against retrospective lodgements
activities.description: The Officer reconciles the control log against retrospective lodgements monthly and pursues outstanding lodgements with the Licence Holder. Persistent non-compliance is a breach of the Licence Agreement and is escalated.

activities.l2: Manage a variation to an installation
activities.l3: Identify the parent licence and installation
activities.description: On receipt of a variation the Officer identifies the parent licence and installation and records the variation against it. A variation does not receive a new licence reference.

activities.l2: Manage a variation to an installation
activities.l3: Classify the variation as like-for-like, minor or major
activities.description: Like-for-like changes are recorded only and redirected to the works notification process. Minor variations within the Standard Envelope receive a desktop assessment; major variations, additional assets or a new power requirement receive a full assessment.

activities.l2: Manage a variation to an installation
activities.l3: Review and reissue amended conditions in full
activities.description: Where the variation affects the licence conditions they are reviewed and amended. Amended conditions supersede and must be reissued in full rather than as a delta.

activities.l2: Manage a variation to an installation
activities.l3: Issue a deed of variation where the extent changes materially
activities.description: Where the variation materially changes the extent of the installation, Legal and Commercial are engaged to issue a deed of variation to the Licence Agreement.

activities.l2: Manage a variation to an installation
activities.l3: Recalculate the annual fee from the variation completion date
activities.description: An assessment fee applies to minor and major variations, and the annual licence fee is recalculated where the number of attachments changes, effective from the completion date of the variation works.

activities.l3: Maintain the installation register and its status
activities.description: The Officer maintains one row per installation recording licence reference, asset IDs, licence holder, equipment schedule, approved conditions, completion date, annual fee, status, last access date and delegated parties.

activities.l3: Maintain the equipment schedule for each installation
activities.description: The equipment schedule is carried from the approved Expression of Interest and updated as varied, recording the individual attachments on the asset.

activities.l3: Reconcile approved submissions against installation records
activities.description: The register is derived manually from approved Expressions of Interest and is not automatically maintained. Installations are known to exist on the network that are not in the register, principally where practical completion was never notified.

activities.l3: Record delegation of authority to act
activities.description: Where a Licence Holder authorises another organisation to act on their behalf, the Officer records the delegating holder, the delegated organisation and ABN, the scope, the date range and the written evidence of authorisation.

activities.l3: Match a new applicant organisation before creating a record
activities.description: The Officer checks whether the organisation already exists before creating an entry, matching on ABN first and then on name, and records the SAP business partner number where one exists. Many applicants have no business partner record.

activities.l3: Record the party roles against the installation
activities.description: Up to four distinct parties may have an interest in one installation — Licence Holder, Equipment Owner, Notifying Party and Billing Party — and for a typical carrier installation on a tower company's licence all four may be different organisations.

activities.l3: Process a change of Licence Holder
activities.description: On sale of a portfolio or corporate restructure the Officer obtains written evidence from both parties, verifies the incoming party's insurance, confirms acceptance of existing conditions, refers to Legal for novation, and advises Finance of the change of Billing Party.

activities.l2: Contact affected parties before asset works
activities.l3: Request a Facilities Access check for planned asset works
activities.description: On scoping asset work the Works Coordinator requests a check by emailing the shared mailbox with the asset IDs and proposed works dates.

activities.l2: Contact affected parties before asset works
activities.l3: Search the register by asset ID to identify installations
activities.description: The Officer searches the Tracker by asset ID. The Tracker is a flat list ordered by submission reference with asset IDs in a free-text column, so the search is unreliable and returns false negatives. Recorded as risk CS-R-097.

activities.l2: Contact affected parties before asset works
activities.l3: Contact each affected Licence Holder with the proposed works
activities.description: The Officer or Works Coordinator provides the licence reference, holder, equipment description, contact details and relevant conditions, contacts each affected holder with the proposed works, dates and required action, and records the response against the installation.

activities.l2: Contact affected parties before asset works
activities.l3: Advise retrospectively where asset work was unplanned
activities.description: Where asset work is unplanned — storm damage, pole failure, emergency replacement — advance contact is not practicable and affected Licence Holders are advised as soon as reasonably possible, and in any case within 2 business days.

activities.l3: Refer apparently abandoned equipment out of the standard procedure
activities.description: Where equipment appears abandoned — no responsive Licence Holder, no licence record, or a holder who declines to remove — it is referred to the unauthorised attachments procedure rather than processed as a decommissioning.

activities.l3: Lodge the Notification of Removal
activities.description: Decommissioning is initiated by the Licence Holder on FRM-FA-04, by SAPN where the licence is terminated for breach or the asset is being removed from service, or by SAPN following expiry of the term without renewal.

activities.l3: Register the decommissioning against the installation and licence
activities.description: The Officer registers the notification and sets the installation status to Decommissioning Notified, then confirms the proposed removal date.

activities.l3: Confirm reinstatement obligations from the licence conditions
activities.description: Reinstatement obligations are confirmed from the licence conditions — typically removal of all brackets and fixings, making good of any penetrations, and removal of identification labelling.

activities.l3: Lodge a Notification of Works for the removal
activities.description: Removal works are themselves a physical access and require a Notification of Works, cleared under the standard process before the removal proceeds.

activities.l3: Verify removal and reinstatement
activities.description: On advice of completion the Officer requests verification by Field Services, by site inspection or by photographic evidence supplied by the Licence Holder, at the Works Coordinator's discretion.

activities.l3: Set the installation to Removed and record the removal date
activities.description: On verified completion the installation status is set to Removed and the removal date recorded.

activities.l3: Notify Finance to cease the annual licence fee
activities.description: The Officer notifies Finance by email to cease the annual licence fee effective the removal date. This is the most frequently missed step in the procedure; failure results in continued billing for a removed installation, a credit, a complaint and potential regulatory exposure.

activities.l3: Reconcile removed installations against active fee records
activities.description: The Officer reconciles removed installations against active fee records quarterly, in both directions — over-billing where the fee was not ceased, and revenue leakage where equipment remains in place.

activities.l3: Terminate the licence where no installations remain
activities.description: Where the licence covers no other installations the Officer requests Team Leader approval to terminate it and advises Legal and Commercial.

activities.l3: Retain the records for the required period
activities.description: Submission, assessment, agreement and correspondence records are retained for the life of the installation plus seven years, and decommissioning records for seven years from removal.
